Best of the day

Every race still to come, in starting-time order. Each card gives the model’s one-line case: the factors it tops and the margin over the second-rated horse; the badge is its rank by Clear, and the top three are highlighted. Tap a card to open the full race.

How the ranking works

Score is the model’s 0–100 merit rating for the card: higher is stronger, but it ranks runners, it is not a probability. Model % turns the score into a win chance across that field — 33.8% means about one win in three. Market % is the same idea read from the prices with the book’s margin removed, so the two chances sit on the same scale; the difference between them is the model’s edge. Break-even price is 1 ÷ model chance: the shortest price at which that chance just pays for itself (33.8% → 2.96). Gap is the score margin over the second-rated horse. Clear divides that gap by the field’s score range, so 20% clear means the gap is a fifth of the whole spread and picks compare across races of any size. Factors is how many model inputs were available; thin cards are not treated as strong evidence.

Unmissable

The model’s absolute standouts: top picks that combine a high rating with a wide, dominant margin over their own field. These are the races worth a closer look before the off.

What makes a horse unmissable?

All five tests must pass: a score of 80 or higher, a gap of at least 15 points to the second-rated horse, a Clear figure of at least 30%, at least six factors available, and a field of at least five runners. Thin-data cards are excluded rather than promoted. This is still a rating, not a guarantee.

Longshots with a chance

A longshot here is 7/1 or bigger on the card, still in the model’s top four, with at least a 4% win chance and with the model chance above the price. The ten biggest edges over the price are listed, in start-time order. A big price is not a tip; the model rank, the chance and the value are the reasons a horse is listed.

Prices are the card prices in this build, not a bookmaker quote. No bet is placed.

Favourites the model doubts

The market favourite is the shortest price in the race. This screen lists the ones the model ranks third or worse, or rates at least five points below the price’s implied chance. It is a disagreement between the model and the market, not a prediction that the horse loses.

Place bankers

The model’s top pick and the market favourite (or joint favourite), with at least a 20% win chance, in a field of five or more. Only a card with a win price can qualify. The model prices wins, not places, so this is a place profile, not a place probability.

Bet slips

Win-only slips built from the model’s top pick in each priced race where the model chance is above the market’s. One leg per race; the strongest edge leads. The straight multiples use the first 2, 3 and 4 legs, the Lucky slips the first 4, 5 and 6, and the full-cover slips the first 3 to 8. Nothing is invented to fill a slip. The each-way section repeats the ladder at two units per bet: a win part and, for GB/IRE legs with standard place terms, a place part; US legs carry only the win part, and a slip with no qualifying leg stays win-only at one unit.

Bet-type reference

The standard composition of the named multiples, including the ones generated above. Every figure is the number of bets, not a recommended stake.

No stake is taken and no bet is placed. Prices are card prices in this build; a real slip may be shorter. If you bet, stake only what you can afford to lose; a multiple loses if any leg loses.

Upcoming slips

The same win-only rule and the same eight-leg limit as Bet slips, but the legs are the races whose post time is still ahead, taken in next-off order rather than by edge. A race only enters once its card carries a price and the model ranks its top pick above the market’s chance. Nothing is invented to fill a slip. The each-way section repeats the ladder at two units per bet; US legs stay win-only.

No stake is taken and no bet is placed. Prices are the card prices in this build; a real slip may be shorter. A multiple loses if any leg loses.

Slip results

The win-only slip rule replayed on settled days from the pre-race card held in this build. A leg is used only when the archived card had a price, the model’s top pick had a positive edge and the stored result names that same pick, so nothing is re-scored after the result. Each slip is settled at its card prices, one unit per bet: a named slip stakes every bet in its structure, and the footer shows what came back against what was staked. Only the page’s settled UK, Irish and US ledger is replayed here; Hong Kong, French and Chilean results live in their own tabs and are not mixed in.

Settled history, not a tip or a staking plan. Card prices are the archived prices, not a quote; returns assume every bet in the structure was staked and win only. No stake is taken and no bet is placed.

Longshot results

Every longshot the Longshots screen flagged on a settled day, replayed from the pre-race card held in this build: a card price of 7/1 or bigger, a top-four model rank, at least a 4% win chance and a model chance above the price. A row enters only when the stored result names the same pick, so nothing is re-scored after the fact. Win bets at one unit, settled at the archived card price; no stake is taken.

Settled history, not a tip. Card prices are the archived prices, not a quote; a real bet may have been shorter. No stake is taken and no bet is placed.

Overhyped results

Every market favourite the Overhyped screen flagged on a settled day, replayed from the pre-race card held in this build: the market made it favourite and the model ranked it third or worse, or rated it at least five points below the price. This is a doubt record, not a bet: it shows how the flagged favourite finished and whether the doubt was justified, with no stake and no P&L. A row enters only when the stored result names the same favourite.

Settled history, not a tip. “Placed” uses the standard place rules recorded with the result and includes wins; “beaten” means the favourite did not win.

Place banker results

Every horse the Place bankers screen flagged on a settled day, replayed from the pre-race card held in this build: the model’s top pick, the market favourite, at least a 20% win chance and a field of five or more. Each GB/IRE banker is recorded as placed or not under the standard place rules stored with its result; a US banker is recorded on the top three, the page’s US place convention, because US racing has no conventional place market. The model prices wins, not places, so this is a settlement record of a place profile, not a place probability. A row enters only when the stored result names the same pick.

Settled history, not a tip. Place terms are the standard place rules recorded with the result, not a quote from a bookmaker. No stake is taken and no bet is placed.

Hong Kong races

Today’s Hong Kong card, built from the official HKJC race card and declarations: official rating, last-six form, barrier draw and declared weight. The model scores it the same fixed way as every other card; tap a row to open the full field. Once a race is off, its model pick is settled against the official HKJC finishing positions — a race is only settled when every declared runner has a position, and a stored pick is never rewritten. No price is on the card when the pick is made, so the market factor drops; the prices archived once betting opens feed the evidence, not the score.

Hong Kong market: HKJC cards are filed before betting opens, so a Hong Kong pick is scored on the factors the card carries and not on the price. Win odds are now archived from twenty minutes before each off; none has been filed yet, so no Hong Kong market factor can be tested.

Model notes 12 November build

  • The rebalance was tested before it shipped. Form drops from 24 to 15, official rating rises from 10 to 15 and Topspeed from 8 to 12, and the whole set was re-run over these 21 races. Winners found stayed at 11, but the winner now sits in the top five 19 times instead of 18 and the top pick placed 15 times instead of 14. Heavier versions were worse, not better: rating 22, form 10 and Topspeed 18 found only 9 winners.
  • It is a favourite-follower. The sheet's top pick won 11 of 21 races; the starting-price favourite won 13. On today's evidence you would have done better backing the shortest price than following this model.
  • Every winner it missed was 5/1 or bigger — 5/1, 11/2, 17/2, 11/1 and 18/1 — and in two of those five it had the winner 6th or worse in the field (the others were 4th, 4th and 5th of their fields). The improving longshot is the blind spot.
  • The factors that would have found them are the ones it trusts least. Diamond Grace took the Market Rasen 15:01 at 17/2 scoring 93 of 100 on official rating and 89 on Topspeed, but only 33 on the rating factor and nothing from the tipsters. Even after the rebalance it was only 5th of 8: official rating now carries 15 of the weight and Topspeed 12, against 13 for the rating and 15 for form.
  • It ranks fields well and picks winners poorly. The winner was in its top three 16 times out of 21, and in its top five 19 times, but its top pick won only 11. The ordering near the head of a race is noisier than the ratings suggest.
  • A scoring bug was live in the morning sheet and is fixed. The tipster factor could go negative for horses nobody tipped (as low as −300), pushing unbacked runners down harder than intended. Correcting it reordered at least two races: total winners fell from 12 to 11, and at Thurles 15:15 the 18/1 winner Duke Otto dropped from 3rd to 8th. The corrected model is, if anything, more of a favourite-follower — so the verdict above is not flattered by the fix.

How the rating works

Twelve factors, fixed weights, one score per horse. Nothing is tuned per race or per card, so two identical horses always get the same rating.

A country earns a tab only when a machine-readable card and a definitive result both name the field; the rows marked on page are the ones wired today. A feed that is blocked, HTML-only or results-only is recorded here rather than shown as an empty tab.

How the rating is calculated

Each factor is scored 0–100 and averaged with fixed weights. Nothing is user-adjustable, so every horse in every race is treated identically. The eleven GB/IE factors total 100; Draw adds 4 where a card carries it, so the full array has twelve entries and 104 nominal weight. The scorer divides by the active weight, so these are relative weights and the effective shares always total 100.

Market (18)
Implied probability from the price, scaled so the shortest-priced runner scores 100.
Form (15)
Last six finishing positions, most recent weighted heaviest, blended 65/35 with how often the horse actually hits the frame. No top-three finish in its last six caps it at 55; one run caps it at 68, two at 76; no form scores 30.
Tipsters (5)
How many of the card's tipsters have put the horse up, normalised across the field. Naps are shown in brackets next to the count but are not scored separately — a nap is one tipster's strongest view, not an extra vote.
Card rating (13)
The rating printed on the card — Racing Post Rating on horseracing.net cards, Timeform on Racing TV cards — normalised across the field. One rating product is used per race, never a mix of the two.
Official rating (15)
The handicapper's view of ability, normalised across the field.
Course & trip (10)
Whether it has won at the track and over the distance. A record like 1/3 is used as a rate; Y/N flags score 72/38.
Draw (4)
Post position; used where the card carries a draw (US/HK), absent on GB/IE cards so the factor drops.
Topspeed (12)
Speed figure, normalised across the field.
Won last time out (4)
Whether the horse won its latest start: Y scores 72, N scores 28. Cards that do not carry the flag drop the factor rather than guessing at the going.
Fitness (3)
Days since last run: peak at 15–35, penalised for long absences and quick reappearances.
Weight (2)
Lower weight scores higher — the point of a handicap.
Stable form (3)
Trainer and jockey 30-day strike rates, straight from the card.

Missing data: if a factor has no figure for a horse, or is identical for the whole field, it is dropped and the other weights renormalise for that runner. A race with no prices is ranked without the market at all, and says so.

Hong Kong market: HKJC cards are filed before betting opens, so a Hong Kong pick is scored on the factors the card carries and not on the price. Win odds are now archived from twenty minutes before each off; none has been filed yet, so no Hong Kong market factor can be tested.

The Model percentage: the 0–100 rating turned into a win chance across the field (a softmax with a fixed scale of 0.04, fitted on 2,251 held-out races). It is a display figure: the selection is still the highest rating, and the ranking does not move with it.

What this is not: a forecast. It has no sectional times, no video, no gallops reports and no stable information. It applies the same reasoning consistently to every runner on the card — it does not make it correct.

Race Sheet is a fixed-weight rating model. Cards and results refresh automatically; the Model percentage is a calibrated win chance from the model's own rating, not a bookmaker probability, and the Market column is the chance the price implies.
